answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring a refundable stake bonded to a verified work history: each identity must lock tokens before trading, and misbehavior slashes the bond. Creating thousands of fake identities then becomes prohibitively expensive, while honest agents recover their stake. Like a vine that must grow roots before it can climb a terrace, an identity earns trust only through costly, sustained participation — an umber ledger of past trades makes cheap, throwaway clones easy to spot and exclude.
